title: Hardware Design Engineer
leads: Nobody. You own the rig and the mount that every worker wears.
where: Cairo. The store, and the site floors where the rigs are worn
hours: Daytime, six days a week. On site when a mount needs testing
summary: You design the rig every worker wears, and you fix the faults that keep coming back.

posting.headline: Hardware Design Engineer (rigs and mounts), Cairo
posting.about: We film real work with small cameras that workers wear on a cap. The footage trains robots. You design the rig and the mount that hold the camera. They must see what the eyes see, sit well for a full shift, last, and stay safe on site.
do: Design the rigs and the mounts. Improve them one step at a time.
Find why a fault keeps coming back. Fix the cause, not just the part.
Design a new mount when a new kind of workplace needs one.
Test every change on a real head, on a site floor, before every site gets it.
Listen to the operators. What slips, hurts, or breaks shapes the next version.
Agree the kit contents and dates with the Head of Deployment.
Send procurement in China a drawing they can make. Parts come through Mano.
need: You have designed or built physical parts: mounts, brackets, or holders.
Able to take a broken part, find why it broke, and change the design.
Able to draw a part and explain it in plain words to a supplier abroad.
Comfortable on a factory or warehouse floor, watching how a rig is really worn.
plus: You have made your own test pieces with a 3D printer or hand tools.
You have worked with a supplier abroad on a made-to-order part.
offer: A steady monthly wage, paid on time.
A weekly design review with the CPO, who owns the hardware.
Your design on every head at every site we run.
A clear job: one rig that sees what the eyes see and lasts.
posting.apply: Send your name, where you live, a phone number, and photos of something you designed and built. We call back within two working days.

offer.heading: Offer of employment
paragraphs: We are pleased to offer you the position of Hardware Design Engineer at KMSC. You will report to {manager}, the CPO.
Your start date is {start}. Your first week is with the rigs in use: the store, a site floor, the fault log. Then the design is yours.

terms.v: Cairo. The store, and the site floors where the rigs are worn

terms.v: Daytime, six days a week. On site when a mount needs testing

conditions: A copy of your national ID.
Your signature on the rules, the consent form, and the fraud briefing.
One account in your own name. Accounts are never shared.
Your first design review, signed off by {manager}.
expect: A fault that keeps coming back gets a cause and a fix, not more spares.
Every change is tried on a real head before every site gets it.
No mount changes a certified helmet or moves the camera off the head.
offer.closing: Please sign below to accept this offer. We look forward to working with you.

handbook.purpose: The client pays for hours filmed from the worker's own point of view. The rig sets that point of view before anyone taps record. A mount that slips costs a flag, and a mount that hurts comes off. You design the rig so that does not happen, and you fix the cause when it does.
outcomes: Every rig sees what the eyes see, all shift, on a cap or a helmet.
A fault that repeats across many phones gets a cause and a changed design.
A new kind of workplace has a working mount before its launch day.
Every version lasts longer than the last.
daily: Morning. Go through yesterday's hardware faults from the wrap reports. Log each by part and site.
Same day. Many rigs at one site share one fault. You get photos and a count. Go.
On site. Watch the rig on a real head at fit, at a reset, at 4:00 PM.
All day. Everyday hardware fixes. Swap the part, then find out why it broke.
weekly: Once a week. Design review with Aly: the fault log, the next change, what to order.
Once a week. Ask the operators what slips, hurts, or breaks. That sets the next version.
monthly: Go through the month's fault log with Aly. Close the causes that repeat.
Send procurement in China the changes for the next order.
standards: The camera sees what the worker's eyes see. Not the floor, not the body, not the ceiling.
A rig sits well for a full shift. A mount that hurts comes off.
The mount goes on the cap or a certified helmet, and never changes the helmet.
A part that breaks twice the same way is a design fault, not bad luck.
Nothing on a rig can cut, catch, or fall on a worker.
never: Never change a certified helmet to fit a mount.
Never send a new mount to every site before a full shift on one head.
Saying the client's name or the app's name outside the company ends the job.

firstMonth.what: The rigs in use. Fit ten with an operator. Watch a full shift.
The store with Mano and Mazen: kit list, spares, fault log.
One fault that keeps coming back. Find the cause. Show Aly the fix.
Your first changed part, tested on a site floor. Aly signs you off.

measures: Hardware faults per 100 mounts a month. Lower every version.
Angle and slipped-mount flags across all sites. Lower every version.
Days from a repeat fault to a changed design.
New kinds of workplaces with a working mount by launch day.
handbook.call: Aly for design and anything you cannot fix. Mano for parts, spares, and orders. Mazen for the next kit. Youssef Medhat when flags point at a mount. Someone hurt by a rig: Moharam now.
